correctness.rationale: The unit-cell matrix kernel differs from the continuous Hardy-phase commutator by a uniformly Hilbert–Schmidt operator (the j,k cell squared error is summable). The logarithmic unitary identifies a finite causal convolution with explicit rational Fourier multiplier. The finite Gram/compressed full-line Gram difference is positive trace class with uniformly bounded trace; cyclic-kernel integration proves every fixed trace moment. Uniform Hilbert–Schmidt discretization error changes finite trace moments by o(log N). Compact-support weighted moment convergence yields fixed-positive-level counts. The quartic roots and Fourier-measure normalization were independently checked; 70 standalone finite checks passed. No finite test is used to infer an infinite limit.

Historical special-case priority remains a genuine residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact number of singular values above every fixed positive threshold grows as a computable constant times log N; this captures effective rank and finite-section approximation costs, rather than a single norm. A genuine splitting of the nonzero superlevel region appears at |ω|=1, with an exact transition interval in threshold t and a one-parameter continuum of explicitly testable coefficients. The phenomenon is motivated by unitary phase modulation of canonical Cesàro smoothing; its full moment law and density do not follow from operator norms alone.
